claim: Extra match between cue and trace does not reliably help; what predicts cue power is how specifically the cue points to the target (diagnostic value, few competitors).
agent_test: Store the same facts under one unique key, unique plus shared key, and two unique keys; measure retrieval hit rate at equal tokens.

claim: Match still helps when competition is held constant (weak intralist cues beat strong extralist cues at equal overload); 'match is a myth' is too strong. Match is the numerator, competition the denominator.
agent_test: Cross query-note overlap (high/low) with number of rival notes sharing the cue (low/high); expect an interaction.

claim: The classic finding that strong extralist cues fail (Thomson and Tulving 1970) is largely a report-bias and monitoring effect: with forced report strong cues work (.26 vs .28 weak).
agent_test: Compare agent retrieval with confidence-gated abstention vs forced candidate listing; count correct items withheld.

claim: Pair-level uniqueness of the encoded relation, not co-presence, sets cue power for associations (cued recall 14.3 vs 5.2 of 24) but not for single-item recognition.
agent_test: Write notes with a distinctive relation sentence vs a generic one; test cued retrieval and item recognition.

claim: Environmental context reinstatement helps modestly on average (d=.28) and shrinks when strong associative processing is present (outshining: d=.13 vs .33); some failed replications are explained by this moderator, but the test-type prediction failed.
agent_test: Add or drop a session tag on stored notes, with and without a strong semantic key; expect tag gain only without the strong key.

claim: Context effects grow with long retention intervals, i.e. when other cues have faded.
agent_test: Test tag benefit at short vs long gap between write and read (many intervening writes).

claim: Cue overload is real in machines: accuracy falls with more items per cue in dense retrievers, LLM key-value streams, and RAG prompts with related distractors.
agent_test: Vary number of rival notes per key (1,4,16); measure answer accuracy; compare a keep-unique policy at equal tokens.

claim: Similar-but-wrong context hurts far more than dissimilar noise, yet random unrelated documents raised RAG accuracy in 2024 small open models (+0.07 absolute, +35% relative at the peak, on a base near 0.2; +1.7 to +3.3 points for junk text in a second study). Mechanism unknown (attention entropy is a hypothesis). No replication on 2025-2026 models was found.
agent_test: Run lexically close vs random vs no distractors; measure accuracy change; do not copy 'add noise'.

claim: Literal match is a crutch: removing word overlap between question and needle makes long-context recall collapse; restoring overlap restores it (Llama 3.3 70B two-hop 25.9 to 87.2 at 32K with literal match, format also changes).
agent_test: Query notes with paraphrase vs verbatim cue; measure the drop; test write-time addition of likely query vocabulary.

claim: Rare and distinctive tokens are better keys than learned semantic similarity for entity lookups: BM25 72.0 vs DPR 49.7 top-20 on EntityQuestions; the gap shrinks for common entities.
agent_test: Keep an exact-term route for ids and names beside the semantic route; compare hit rate on rare vs common entities.

claim: Weighting handles by rarity (IDF, HippoRAG node specificity) gives a measurable but modest gain (average R@5 72.9 vs 67.8 without).
agent_test: Ablate an IDF-style weight in the agent's retrieval at fixed k.

claim: Neither pure lexical nor pure single-vector retrieval suffices: embeddings have capacity limits, and BM25 collapses (-89%) under synonym substitution.
agent_test: Hybrid lexical plus semantic vs either alone on a synonym-shifted query set.

claim: Adding a distinguishing context line to each stored chunk at write time cuts failed retrievals in three sources (Anthropic vendor blog 5.7% to 1.9%; Yousuf 2026 Context@5 33.3 to 55.0 on repetitive SEC chunks; RaMem 2026). The nearest control, RaMem's shuffle test, shows wrong tags are worse than none. No same-length filler prefix arm exists in any of them. Stern and Nadel 2026 (dual-trace scene written at storage): 73.7% vs 53.5% on 99 LongMemEval-S questions, +20.2 pp, but only in temporal, update and multi-session tasks, 0 pp in single-session; one run per arm, no filler arm and no write-versus-read ablation. Newer evidence: appending a fact line to the key beat the plain key in LongMemEval (Recall@10 .784 vs .692 round, .862 vs .783 session) but a condensed key alone lost; no equal-length filler arm exists.
agent_test: Contextualised vs plain vs same-length filler prefix on notes.

claim: In transformers, keys decide what is retrieved: swapping K only leaves facts present but unretrievable (30-40% accuracy); swapping K and V gives 100% counterfactual answers.
agent_test: Not testable on a black-box agent; motivation only.

claim: Position acts as a cue: relevant info in the middle of context is used worse; contrasting needles are easier; focused short context beats full context.
agent_test: Place the retrieved note at start/middle/end; compare focused vs full context at equal tokens.

claim: Telling the model to ignore or forget competing items gives weak or inconsistent gains; sampling and voting, or changing what is stored, works better.
agent_test: Compare an 'ignore irrelevant' instruction vs voting vs pre-filtering at equal tokens.

claim: Humans are less sensitive to fan than dense retrieval (slope .41 vs .67), HippoRAG in between (.44); the mechanism is not separated. Preprint with id/date oddity.
agent_test: Low confidence until the source is checked.

claim: No direct LLM test of outshining or of Nairne-style cue distinctiveness at equal tokens was found. Closest: Stern and Nadel 2026 (extra write-time scene helps only where one plain cue was not enough, none in single-session lookup, 0 pp, CI -15 to +15) and RaMem 2026 (tag shuffle test). Neither removes a strong semantic key on purpose.
agent_test: Design: shared vs unique cue words x with/without strong cue, at equal tokens.

claim: Wrong tags are worse than no tags: shuffling session and time metadata across stored memories (same content, same length) cut ground-truth Recall@10 from 0.8066 to 0.2358 (GPT-4.1-mini) while removing session context gave 0.5708.
agent_test: Shuffle tags across notes in the agent store and compare with no tags at equal tokens.

claim: On conversational agent memory (LoCoMo), plain cosine beats BM25 by 16 points (73.4 vs 57.1) and a hybrid pool with an LLM reranker is best (77.2); write strategy matters 3-8 points, retrieval 14-23. No ratio-rule or IDF-variant test exists on agent memory.
agent_test: Compare cosine, BM25, ratio score (target over summed rival similarity) and IDF-weighted cosine on the agent's own store at fixed k.

claim: Tool and file based search beat one-shot RAG on a long agent-memory benchmark (72.5 vs 48.5), and embedding search alone fails to chain linked evidence (6% vs 44% on one task). Neither tests literal overlap.
agent_test: Run NoLiMa-style paraphrased queries against an external store with grep plus embedding tools.

claim: LLMs under-abstain with retrieved text rather than over-withhold: on insufficient context Claude 3.5 Sonnet abstained 84.1% without RAG and 52% with it; GPT-4o 34.4 to 31.2; Gemini 1.5 Pro 100 to 18.6. Selective generation lifts accuracy among answered by 2-10%. The Higham forced-listing recovery was not measured. Counter-evidence: with only irrelevant chunks, 7-8B models over-refuse questions they can answer, and over-abstention reaches .259 for Claude-Sonnet-4 on a small benchmark (LIT-RAGBench). Both errors occur.
agent_test: Compare confidence-gated retrieval to forced candidate listing on the agent's store and count correct candidates withheld.

claim: Poirier-type results have been repeated outside the original lab with accuracy: Goh and Lu 2012 (NUS, 3 experiments) and Badham 2016 Exp 2 (recall accuracy, 30 young and 31 older adults; shared author). No failed replication and no preregistered replication was found.
agent_test: None (human result).

claim: Original numbers of Tulving and Thomson 1973 and Thomson and Tulving 1970 remain unverified (paywalled). Watkins and Tulving 1975 Exp 3 numbers are verified second-hand from Tulving and Wiseman 1975 full text: recall .63 vs recognition .32, recognised and recalled .26, recalled only .37.
agent_test: Cite only the verified Tulving-Wiseman figures; do not quote 1973 percentages.

claim: Softmax attention acts like a ratio rule: with 100 distractors, adding 10% hard distractors cut attention on the gold document from 97% to 21% (128K context, three open models). This is an analogy to Nairne's diagnostic ratio, not a test of it.
agent_test: Place close near-duplicate notes versus unrelated notes in the prompt at equal tokens and compare accuracy.

claim: Recognition failure of recallable words is a general effect, not a one-off: it was found in word lists (12 experiments, 40 conditions), in a replication that tested the generate-recognize rival, and in well-known melodies.
agent_test: Probe each stored fact with its copy (restated) and with its original cue; count facts found by one route only. Expect a sizeable one-route-only share.

claim: The clean Tulving-Wiseman function (c=.50, r=.95) is an aggregate artefact: failure concentrates in items whose cue and target are related outside the study episode, and pooled subject data inflate dependence (subject-wise r=.59 vs item-wise r=-.03).
agent_test: Score memory tests per item, not pooled; list the facts where the key fails and check what they share.

claim: Recall beating recognition is not a stable result: Postman (1975) Exp 2 did not find it, and it reverses for some word types.
agent_test: None needed at agent level; use only as a warning that copy-match checks can be weaker than cue-based search.

claim: Direction of the pre-existing link matters: cue-to-target association helps recall only, target-to-cue helps recognition only (Fisher 1979, F about 52 vs about 1). Generative encoding makes both directions work equally (Ley 1977).
agent_test: Build index keys from the direction the future query arrives from; test question-shaped vs item-shaped keys at equal tokens.

claim: The way an item is processed at write time sets which later queries succeed: trait judgment of faces gave 55% vs 25% recognition but worse feature reconstruction (Wells and Hryciw, N=80); unique-relation encoding gave 14.3 vs 5.2 of 24 pairs (Stein).
agent_test: Store each note in two forms (summary, verbatim) and test queries of both kinds; check whether form x query type crosses over.

claim: A strong generic category cue given only at test still helps (62.8 vs 35.8 percent recall for categorised input; heading at recall alone 57.1 vs 26.1), and strong output cues beat weak ones whatever the input cue was. The strict copy-match reading fails.
agent_test: At query time, add a broad category word to the query; compare against the stored-tag-only condition.

claim: Context cues work when item-bound, rare or when no better cue exists: GPS context benefit d=.44 for rare places vs .15 for common; VR benefit only for items useful in the scene (beta .52 vs .18, ns); place effect only at 1.5 s study (d' 1.47 vs .74) not at 4 s.
agent_test: Compare a generic session tag with a content-bound tag, on notes with and without strong semantic keys, at equal tokens.

claim: Dual-trace encoding (a concrete scene stored beside each fact) gave +20.2 pp on LongMemEval-S with Claude Sonnet 4.6 and about equal token cost, with the gain only where one cue was insufficient.
agent_test: Replicate with a same-length neutral filler arm and a write-only vs read-only ablation, 20+ questions per category.

claim: Using the first retrieved unit as a new cue to pull missing evidence (associative recollection) improves agent memory: LoCoMo judge 87.14 vs 83.83 for the best baseline, with about 1,472 answer tokens; removing components costs 3.2 to 4.6 percent relative.
agent_test: Two-hop retrieval, where hit one is used to query again, vs single-hop at equal answer tokens.

claim: Generate-recognize survives as a two-stage view only in revised form: relational (broad) encoding boosts generation, item-specific encoding boosts recognition. The original pipeline predicted near 1.00 recognition of recallable items and failed.
agent_test: Broad key to produce candidates plus a distinct detail check; vs one key alone.

claim: Probing a memory by one route may change what a second route finds, so test order is a confound in recall-recognition independence.
agent_test: Randomise probe order in agent memory tests.

claim: A distinctive key works as an addition to the raw text, not a replacement: condensed keys alone (fact, summary, keyphrase) lost to the raw text key, while raw text plus extracted facts won (LongMemEval_M Recall@10 .784 vs .692 round; .862 vs .783 session). Keyphrase alone was worst (.392 round).
agent_test: Compare raw note, tag only, raw plus tag, raw plus same-length neutral line, at equal key length.

claim: The gain from extra distinctive keys is largest where the plain retriever is weakest (fact expansion Recall@5, session: BM25 +.049, Contriever +.039, Stella +.012; round: +.082, +.023, -.016). Consistent with outshining, but retriever and model are confounded and the design is not crossed.
agent_test: Cross tag present/absent with a strong or deliberately degraded plain key on the agent's own notes.

claim: When the later query is semantically disconnected from the stored cue, all tested memory methods collapse (LoCoMo-Plus: embedding RAG 15.55, Mem0 15.80, A-Mem 17.20, gpt-4o full context 21.05, gemini-2.5-pro 26.06), the machine analogue of encoding-retrieval mismatch.
agent_test: Write an intent-level second key per note and measure hits on trigger queries that share no words with the note.

claim: Storing hypothetical questions beside a chunk helps most when many similar chunks compete (QuOTE SQuAD C@1 90.03 vs 79.31; relative gain rising from about 8 to over 20 percent with more contexts); HyDE gave no gain (76.60) at about 10 times the query cost. No length-matched control, so extra-text effects are not excluded.
agent_test: Index each note by its raw text, by a likely-question line, and by a summary line; score on queries phrased as questions and as task needs.

claim: Generated index keys must be supported by the item: unfiltered Doc2Query queries hurt, and dropping the least relevant 30 percent raised RR@10 from .277 to .316 while shrinking the index by about a third.
agent_test: Audit generated tags against their notes and compare retrieval with and without the unsupported ones.

claim: No source found measures the encoding-versus-retrieval split of Stern and Nadel's +20.2 pp, a same-length filler arm, a Nairne ratio score on agent memory, or an accuracy replication of Poirier 2012 outside its network; these gaps stay open.
agent_test: Run the ablations listed in critique.md gaps 1, 2 and 3.
